messages.author: c4390b997ff96dbb
messages.subject: merge multiple chr into 1
parts:
Hi,

I am working with 9 linkage groups from the ‘formLinkageGroups’ analysis.

Based on previous work, I am able to assign chr=1, chr=8, chr=9 to a single chromosome and  chr=3, chr=4, chr=5, chr=7 map to another chromosome.

I would like to run the analysis with just with the markers on chr 1, 8, 9 [and then chr 3,4,5,7] to see if I can get them to group together into one large linkage group.

I need help with the code.

This is what I’ve tried:

 

All_q50C50trim <- formLinkageGroups(All_q50C50trim, max.rf=0.35, min.lod=8, reorgMarkers=TRUE)

lg9 <- orderMarkers(All_q50C50trim, chr=9)

lg8 <- orderMarkers(All_q50C50trim, chr=8)

lg1 <- orderMarkers(All_q50C50trim, chr=1)

#All_q50C50trimCHR2 <- orderMarkers(All_q50C50trim, c(lg9, lg8, lg1))

 

OR

 

All_q50C50trim <- formLinkageGroups(All_q50C50trim, max.rf=0.35, min.lod=8, reorgMarkers=TRUE)

All_q50C50trimCHR2 <- orderMarkers(All_q50C50trim[, c(chr=9, chr=8, chr=1)])

 

thanks. roberta

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] merge multiple chr into 1
parts: You might just force all of the markers in linkage groups 1,8,9 to be in the same linkage group, by moving the markers on linkage groups 8 and 9 to linkage group 1:

mn <- markernames(All_q50C50trim, chr=c(8,9))
for(marker in mn)
All_q50C50trim <- movemarker(All_q50C50trim, marker, 1)

Then do the same for 3,4,5,7, moving the markers from 4,5,7 to lg 3:

mn <- markernames(All_q50C50trim, chr=c(4,5,7))
for(marker in mn)
All_q50C50trim <- movemarker(All_q50C50trim, marker, 3)

karl
